name: Shodan
what: A search engine for internet-connected devices. It shows which ports, services, banners and certificates are visible on public IP addresses.
when: To see your organization's internet exposure the way an outsider does, and to monitor your own public IP ranges for newly exposed services.
cost_note: A free account gives limited searching; a one-time membership and monthly API plans unlock more results, filters and IP monitoring.
example: Create an account and search for your organization's public IP addresses or domain name.
Open each result and note the open ports, product banners and certificate details.
Compare the list with what you intend to expose; anything unexpected (RDP, management interfaces, old VPN portals) is a finding.
On a plan that includes it, add your own IP ranges to network monitoring to get alerts on changes.
pitfalls: Results can be days or weeks old; confirm with your own scan before you act.
Some filters and features need a paid membership or plan.
Only monitor IP ranges you own or are responsible for.
